profile.name: Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library
profile.tagline: Inspiring leadership, conservation, and courageous citizenship through the life and legacy of Theodore Roosevelt.

items.headline: The Bull Moose Campaign of 1912: The Third-Party Insurgency
items.blurb: After breaking with President Taft over progressive reform, Roosevelt launched a bold third-party run in 1912 as the Bull Moose candidate.

items.headline: Theodore Roosevelt and the Panama Canal, 1903
items.blurb: How Roosevelt got the Panama Canal built: the failed French attempt, Panama’s 1903 revolution, the canal treaty and the locks that opened in 1914.

items.headline: The Holiday Trees at the Library in Medora, North Dakota
items.blurb: Six holiday trees made by North Dakota artisans from ranch leather, lariats, prairie grass, bandanas and clay are on view at the Library in Medora.

items.headline: ​Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library: immersive storytelling & sustainability
items.blurb: The project offers lessons in integrating complex AV, interactive storytelling and environmental performance

items.headline: The Teddy Bear: A Moment of Mercy That Became an Icon
items.blurb: On a 1902 Mississippi hunt, Roosevelt refused to shoot a captive black bear—a moment of mercy that inspired the beloved teddy bear.

items.headline: The African Safari (1909
items.blurb: In 1909, the fifty-year-old former president set off with his son Kermit on a Smithsonian hunting and scientific expedition into the African interior.

items.headline: Roosevelt at Harvard: The Making of a Historian and Political Thinker
items.blurb: Arriving at Harvard in 1876 at seventeen, Theodore brought insatiable curiosity and a body remade by exercise, becoming a historian and political…

items.headline: Edith Kermit Carow Roosevelt
items.blurb: Childhood friends on Manhattan's Union Square, Edith Kermit Carow and Theodore Roosevelt grew inseparable, and she became his wife and First Lady.

items.headline: Alice Hathaway Lee Roosevelt
items.blurb: Born into Boston's Chestnut Hill elite in 1861, Alice Hathaway Lee charmed Theodore during his Harvard years and became his radiant first wife.

items.headline: The New Nationalism (1910)
items.blurb: Roosevelt's progressive manifesto, delivered August 31, 1910 at Osawatomie, Kansas, laying out a bolder vision of government serving the public good.

items.headline: Governor of New York: The Stepping Stone to the Presidency (1899-1900)
items.blurb: Riding fame from the Rough Riders and San Juan Hill, Theodore Roosevelt won the New York governorship in 1898, a key step toward the presidency.

items.headline: How Theodore and Franklin Roosevelt Were Related
items.blurb: Theodore and Franklin Roosevelt were fifth cousins, and Theodore's niece Eleanor married Franklin.

items.headline: Rahm Emanuel: A Fight for the Center and Winning the Lottery of Life
items.blurb: Rahm Emanuel has never been shy about being in the arena, whether as White House Chief of Staff, an Illinois congressman, Chicago mayor, or…

items.headline: The Roosevelt White House: Renovation, Power, and Family Chaos
items.blurb: In 1902 Roosevelt hired McKim, Mead & White to modernize the White House and build the West Wing, all amid a house full of romping children.

items.headline: A Day in the Life of Young Theodore: Inside the Life of an Extraordinary Boy
items.blurb: Follow eleven-year-old Theodore Roosevelt through a single 1870 day, waking before dawn in his family's Manhattan townhouse to keep his own ambitious…

items.headline: Theodore Roosevelt's Presidency
items.blurb: Step inside Roosevelt's presidency — the Square Deal, the Panama Canal, trust-busting, and a bully pulpit that redefined what the office could do.

items.headline: Theodore Roosevelt in New York Politics
items.blurb: Roosevelt's first years in politics — a cyclone in the Albany Assembly at twenty-three, and the single February day in 1884 that changed his life…

items.headline: Edith Kermit Carow Roosevelt: The Partner Who Made the Presidency Possible
items.blurb: Edith Carow grew up alongside young Theodore in New York's Union Square, becoming the steady partner who helped make his presidency possible.

items.headline: Midwinter Table
items.blurb: An evening of Badlands food and drink–with the people who make it.

items.headline: The Assassination Attempt: Milwaukee, October 14, 1912
items.blurb: A delusional gunman shot Roosevelt in Milwaukee on October 14, 1912, an attempt that became one of the most dramatic moments of his campaign.
